# MAG 7 Daily
> **Nvidia will invest three billion dollars in Meta to scale Muse agents.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nvidia will invest three billion dollars in Meta’s equity offering and the two companies are expanding work on Muse, including more Vera Rubin hardware. Microsoft opened a voluntary exit to about 60,000 eligible employees in four countries. Apple unveiled the iPad mini that had circulated as an OLED rumor, now with a shipping design, chip and price.

### Top News
**Nvidia puts $3 billion into Meta and expands the Muse partnership: NVIDIA Newsroom**
Nvidia will invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering, a planned commitment rather than a completed sale, as the companies expand work on Muse and the Muse family of models to improve training and inference and to cut the cost of running those systems. Meta intends to expand deployment of Nvidia Vera Rubin systems and Vera CPUs for next-generation agents, plus Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4. The companies are also considering Nvidia’s OpenShell Reference Architecture for safer agent deployment and Sentry for monitoring agent behavior. Jensen Huang said agents are a new computing paradigm and that the partnership is meant to optimize infrastructure so Muse can serve billions of people. Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is how Meta brings personal superintelligence to everyone. Nvidia said Muse models and agents on its infrastructure have delivered frontier-level benchmark performance and surging consumer downloads since launch. Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-meta-to-expand-collaboration-on-muse-and-muse-family-of-models-amid-robust-growth) · [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/nvidia-invests-3-billion-meta-deeper-ai-partnership) · [grafa.com](https://grafa.com/en/news/united-states/nvidia-meta-3-billion-investment-ai-partnership)

**Microsoft opens a voluntary exit to about 60,000 employees: Instant Gaming News**
An internal memo from chief people officer Amy Coleman launched a time-limited voluntary separation programme for eligible employees at level 70 and below on participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States, about 60,000 people, roughly a quarter of the workforce. Coleman said it lets people who want a future outside Microsoft leave with support and gives participating organizations another way to match staffing to changing needs; some organizations are not offering it, and it builds on a voluntary programme earlier this year. Eligible people were to get an email with the terms. In India, where Microsoft has about 23,000 employees and eligibility was not broken out, the decision deadline is December 1, and the package is understood to match standard severance: one month of base salary per completed year, plus health insurance and career-transition services. A Microsoft spokesperson said the company is backing India’s AI ambitions with $20.5 billion committed from 2025 through 2029 and is on track to equip 20 million people in India with AI skills by 2030. Source: [news.instant-gaming.com](https://news.instant-gaming.com/en/articles/22684-microsoft-announces-a-voluntary-buyout-to-60-000-employees) · [hdfcsky.com](https://hdfcsky.com/news/microsoft-announces-voluntary-exit-offer-for-employees-in-india-3-other-countries)

**Apple unveils the iPad mini that had been an OLED rumor: The Hindu**
Apple unveiled the new iPad mini, calling it the biggest update ever: 5.4 millimetres thin, with an 8.5-inch OLED display, peak brightness of 1,200 nits, 600 nits full-screen for SDR and HDR, a 1-nit minimum and a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. It runs the A20 Pro with a 7-core GPU and neural accelerators in each GPU core; IOL reported the CPU up to 60 percent faster and the GPU about 2.7 times the prior model, with doubled memory bandwidth, and a 512GB model that adds a core on the CPU and dual 16-core Neural Engines. The tablet is IP67, rated for 1 metre for 30 minutes, with a 12-megapixel landscape front camera, a 12-megapixel wide back camera, Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 frames per second. Storage is 128GB, 256GB and 512GB, in Midnight and Starlight; the US price starts at $699, and in India Wi-Fi starts at ₹82,900, Wi-Fi plus cellular at ₹1,00,900, and education pricing at ₹76,900. Pre-orders open October 28 and sales begin November 6. Battery life is up to 10 hours, with a 50 percent charge in about 30 minutes on a 35-watt or higher adapter. Dave Pakula, vice president of Hardware Engineering, called it a huge leap for a full iPad in the palm of the hand. Siri AI arrives in beta with iPadOS 27. Source: [thehindu.com](https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/technology/apple-unveils-new-ipad-mini-with-thinner-design/article71630115.ece) · [iol.co.za](https://iol.co.za/technology/gadgets/2026-10-27-apple-unveils-redesigned-thinner-ipad-mini-with-oled-display/)

### Company Desk
**Apple ships iOS 27.2 with Siri recall and more than 160 fixes: MacRumors**
Apple released iOS 27.2, the first major iOS 27 update, putting the iPhone Duo and other iPhones on the same version. Siri AI can recall past conversations and draw on photos attached to Messages, calendar-event attendees and voicemails, with better results from Safari history and Reading List; it requires an iPhone 15 Pro or later, remains unavailable in the EU and mainland China, and adds French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish. The update addresses more than 160 security vulnerabilities, none of which Apple said were actively exploited. Multiview in the Apple TV app now runs on iPhone for up to four live sports streams at once, covering MLS, Formula 1 in the US, and Friday Night Baseball doubleheaders. The Apple Music icon is now black and white, replacing the red mark. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/26/ios-27-2-features/)

**Meta lays out a stock sale of up to $97.5 billion for AI: Telecompaper**
Meta plans to sell up to $97.5 billion in stock to fund its AI ambitions, starting with $37.5 billion of Class A stock and new depositary shares based on preferred stock. The other $60 billion may be raised over time through a programme to sell Class C shares from the first quarter of 2027. The Times of India reported the sale is structured so Mark Zuckerberg can raise money without surrendering voting control, and that Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom are interested in buying shares. Source: [telecompaper.com](https://www.telecompaper.com/news/meta-announces-plans-to-sell-up-to-usd-95-billion-in-new-shares-to-fund-ai-plans--1586818) · [timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/meta-plans-to-raise-up-to-95-billion-for-its-ai-expansion-through-two-stock-offerings-with-nvidia-amd-and-broadcom-interested-in-buying-shares-as-mark-zuckerberg-seeks-new-funding-without-surrendering-voting-control/articleshow/135226925.cms)

### Also Today
**JAŸ-Z to headline the 2027 Apple Music Super Bowl show: 9to5Mac**
The NFL and Apple Music said JAŸ-Z will headline the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium, with the US broadcast on ABC and ESPN; Apple Music has sponsored the show since 2022. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/26/jay-z-confirmed-as-headliner-for-apple-musics-2027-super-bowl-halftime-show/)

**Older Siri Remotes show up in Find My: MacRumors**
With iOS 27.2 and tvOS 27.2, second- and third-generation Siri Remotes appear in the Find My app, but they still cannot play a sound and do not have Precision Finding. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/26/siri-remote-find-my-ios-27-2/)

**Google says Gemini 4 Argon trails Claude and GPT-6 on Android coding: 9to5Google**
Google says Gemini 4 Argon ranks well behind Claude and GPT-6 for Android coding. Source: [9to5google.com](https://9to5google.com/2026/10/26/android-bench-rankings-gemini-4-argon/)

**Xero connects live books to Gemini: The Fintech Times**
Xero is connecting live financial data to Google Gemini for small and midsize businesses. Source: [thefintechtimes.com](https://thefintechtimes.com/xero-connects-live-financial-data-to-google-gemini-for-smbs/)

**Google Classroom adds Gemini visibility for teachers: EdTech Innovation Hub**
Google is adding Gemini app publishing and teacher insights that let teachers see students’ Gemini notebook conversations. Source: [edtechinnovationhub.com](https://www.edtechinnovationhub.com/news/google-classroom-now-lets-teachers-see-students-gemini-notebook-conversations)

**DeepMind promotes Iason Gabriel: EdTech Innovation Hub**
Google DeepMind promoted Iason Gabriel to principal scientist and director at the DeepMind Institute. Source: [edtechinnovationhub.com](https://www.edtechinnovationhub.com/news/google-deepmind-promotes-iason-gabriel-to-principal-scientist-and-director-at-deepmind-institute)

### The Counterpoint
**Suppliers buying the customer is the circular-capital problem: The Times of India**
The same fundraising that Nvidia is joining is the one The Times of India flags as circular capital: silicon suppliers are eyeing a $5 billion stake while Meta sells shares to fund AI expansion, and Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom are among those interested in buying. A supplier writing a cheque into the customer that then buys that supplier’s systems is not an outside test of demand, and the Times framed Zuckerberg’s aim as new money without giving up voting control. Source: [timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/meta-plans-to-raise-up-to-95-billion-for-its-ai-expansion-through-two-stock-offerings-with-nvidia-amd-and-broadcom-interested-in-buying-shares-as-mark-zuckerberg-seeks-new-funding-without-surrendering-voting-control/articleshow/135226925.cms)

### The Thread: Three cheques, one crowded shelf
Almost a quarter of a trillion dollars is the sum The Information put on three fundraising plans unveiled the same Monday, from Anthropic, SpaceX and Meta. SpaceX signed a $40 billion financing agreement with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management to lease graphics processors, which SpaceX called the largest GPU financing in history. Colleague Alex Eichenstein reported that the money is expected to run through a special purpose vehicle kept off SpaceX’s balance sheet, a structure that could limit any hit to its credit rating. Meta’s board committee, in a filing last week, said timing mattered so the company could secure capital before competitors saturate funding options, and it named a congested pipeline that includes Alphabet, SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI. Microsoft is the other of the seven in that piece, and the new number is take-up rather than eligibility: the global workforce is 223,000, an earlier voluntary offer went to 9,000 people and about a third accepted, and Microsoft is expected to see a smaller share this time, fewer than 20,000.

The shared constraint is the funding shelf, not a shared product. Meta’s directors treated Alphabet’s deals as occupying the same equity and debt options Meta wants to use before they fill up. Microsoft is offering exits while that window is still described as open. The Apollo lease is the article’s exhibit that a company with Elon Musk’s platform is choosing an off-balance-sheet GPU structure rather than a plain borrowing. Musk, in a post on X that The Information quotes, said debt markets in recent weeks have closed to firms whose revenue is only from AI data centers, and that more than 200 neoclouds face what he called guppy-level death and consolidation. The Information notes that the argument is self-serving: fewer neoclouds could leave more capital for SpaceX and other large names later. Apollo’s chief economist, Torsten Slok, wrote over the weekend that despite the investment and the hype, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech.

For Meta, the filing turns the raise into a race against other people’s calendars, including Alphabet’s, rather than a quiet registration. For Microsoft, the buyout math is the operational twin of the same squeeze: on the take-up the company is expected to see, the offer does not empty a quarter of a 223,000-person company. The risk the piece leaves on the table is Slok’s zero, and Musk’s warning that investor disfavor could spread from neoclouds to larger AI companies if customers keep seeing no payoff. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/anthropic-spacex-meta-cash-grabs)

### On the Calendar
Pre-orders for the new iPad mini open on October 28, 2026, with sales beginning November 6. Source: [thehindu.com](https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/technology/apple-unveils-new-ipad-mini-with-thinner-design/article71630115.ece)

Eligible Microsoft employees in India have until December 1, 2026, to decide on the voluntary exit offer. Source: [hdfcsky.com](https://hdfcsky.com/news/microsoft-announces-voluntary-exit-offer-for-employees-in-india-3-other-countries)

Meta’s programme to sell Class C shares may start in the first quarter of 2027, for as much as $60 billion of the AI stock sale. Source: [telecompaper.com](https://www.telecompaper.com/news/meta-announces-plans-to-sell-up-to-usd-95-billion-in-new-shares-to-fund-ai-plans--1586818)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Unilever cut order handling from twenty minutes to ninety seconds for retailers.**

**What You Need to Know:** Unilever cut order handling from twenty minutes to ninety seconds for retailers, using a Microsoft-built agent system now running in production. NVIDIA published a full reference architecture for containing enterprise agents, Mazda put Gemini in a Canadian CX-5, and a New Mexico order plus a California tax arrangement landed on Meta the same week Apple blocked a set of weak web certificates.

### Top News
**Unilever’s multi-agent creating customer value at global scale: Microsoft UK Stories**
Unilever has launched NOVA, five AI agents built with Microsoft on Foundry, to read, check and enter customer orders that still arrive as emails, PDFs, spreadsheets or photos. Microsoft UK Stories reports that about 300,000 direct customers are served, and that 3.7 billion people use a Unilever product every day. Four agents read the message and extract the order; a fifth checks the work. Francis Castro, head of technology for customer operations, says orders in the pilots are eight times faster than before, refund claims are processed twice as fast, and new-customer onboarding has been reduced by 90 percent. Microsoft engineers joined Unilever to build and test claims validation in less than eight weeks. NOVA has already processed thousands of orders in production. Source: [ukstories.microsoft.com](https://ukstories.microsoft.com/features/unilevers-multi-agent-creating-customer-value-at-global-scale/)

**NVIDIA unveils architecture for secure enterprise AI agents: Engineering.com**
NVIDIA today announced the OpenShell Reference Architecture for building, containing and enforcing safe agents, extending the OpenShell secure runtime it had already set out. Engineering.com reports that Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are said to deliver 30 times higher throughput per megawatt on agentic workloads, while Vera CPUs are said to deliver twice the performance of x86 processors and to run the OpenShell boundary. BlueField-4 runs NVIDIA Sentry, which quarantines an agent that leaves its software boundary in milliseconds and boosts agent capacity by up to 20 percent. ServiceNow said Arc, a personal long-running agent, is generally available, with policies carried to OpenShell and Sentry so access can be revoked across software and hardware within seconds. The stack is described as able to run on Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure, including Microsoft Windows via Microsoft Execution Containers, and to host agents from builders including Google, Meta and OpenAI. Source: [engineering.com](https://www.engineering.com/nvidia-unveils-architecture-for-secure-enterprise-ai-agents/)

**Google Gemini Enhances the Connected Driving Experience in the All-New Mazda CX-5: Chinook Observer**
Mazda Canada said on October 26 that Google Gemini is available to eligible users in the all-new CX-5 equipped with Google built-in. Drivers can use everyday language, including follow-up requests, for navigation, Google Maps traffic and recommendations, Spotify and YouTube Music, hands-free messages, and supported vehicle functions such as climate. Tasks started on a smartphone can continue in the car through compatible Google services. Amy Fleming, president and CEO of Mazda Canada, said the aim is technology that stays in the background so the driver stays on the road. Mazda Canada’s retail network is 163 stores. Source: [pr.chinookobserver.com](https://pr.chinookobserver.com/article/Google-Gemini-Enhances-the-Connected-Driving-Experience-in-the-All-New-Mazda-CX-5/6adf095adba4ed9cc76d96b2)

**Apple Addresses Web Security Threat, Working on macOS Update With Additional Fix: MacRumors**
Apple has been blocking eMudhra’s compromised TLS certificates since October 19 in Safari, Mail, and apps that use Apple’s networking and security frameworks, MacRumors reports from Apple’s support document. A researcher found that private keys on eight of the Indian firm’s intermediate certificate-authority certificates were weak; those keys could have allowed impersonation of legitimate sites, and Apple says there is currently no evidence of malicious exploitation. The block is automatic and does not require a software update for most devices. macOS command-line tools can still accept the certificates until a macOS update changes the default /etc/ssl/cert.pem file; until then, administrators can remove the root CA certificates from that file. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/25/apple-blocks-compromised-emudhra-certificates/)

**Meta loses $124bn in value as AI spending plans hit US tech shares: Business Matters**
A New Mexico judge on Wednesday ordered Meta to pay $25 billion over its handling of Facebook user data, and Meta plans to appeal, Business Matters reports. Separately, the board plans to award Mark Zuckerberg, 42, Class C non-voting shares he could sell to pay a possible California billionaire wealth tax without giving up control. He owns about 13 percent of Meta and controls about 61 percent of its votes; he told the board that selling existing shares to pay the tax would cut his voting power to 53 percent. He has pledged to remain living in California for the next eight years. The proposed tax is a one-off 5 percent levy on the assets of any billionaire living in the state on January 1, 2026. A special committee said its negotiations with him were protracted and, at several points, contentious, and concluded that his presence at headquarters in Menlo Park was critical. Source: [bmmagazine.co.uk](https://bmmagazine.co.uk/ai/meta-ai-spending-tech-sell-off/)

### Company Desk
**Springer Nature and Google DeepMind partner on AI peer review assistant: Research Information**
Springer Nature and Google DeepMind have announced a research partnership to build an AI peer-review assistant that helps reviewers navigate manuscripts, charts and figures without replacing human judgement. Research Information reports that a prototype is in test, built with Google’s open-source Agent Development Kit and run inside Springer Nature’s private Gemini Enterprise environment so manuscripts used in development stay on Springer Nature’s infrastructure. The project builds on Google tools including ScholarPeer and Deep Review, and on Springer Nature’s in-house platform Snapp. Saskia Steinacker, chief product officer at Springer Nature, said reviewer expertise remains fundamental and that innovation and trust have to move together. Seshu Ajjarapu, senior director of applied AI at Google DeepMind, said the aim is a review experience that keeps pace with submission volume while holding journal standards. Source: [researchinformation.info](https://www.researchinformation.info/news/springer-nature-and-google-deepmind-partner-on-ai-peer-review-assistant/)

**Apple Display Veterans Step Back as New Leaders Take Over: MacRumors**
Victor Yin now oversees much of Apple’s display development, after years of preparation under Wei Chen and John Zhong, MacRumors reports from Mark Gurman. Chen and Zhong, each with about 30 years at Apple, are moving to more limited roles as advisers, in a succession Gurman describes as underway for several years. October promotions made Rajesh Ambati, Louie Sanguinetti and Derek Shaeffer vice presidents, covering connectivity hardware and software. The shifts follow Apple’s expansion of Johny Srouji’s role to chief hardware officer, putting hardware engineering and hardware technologies under him. Gurman also reports that some hardware program managers have been laid off in recent weeks as Srouji and CEO John Ternus remove management layers. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/26/apple-display-veterans-step-back/)

Source: [prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fileai-signs-strategic-collaboration-agreement-with-aws-to-accelerate-rollout-of-outcome-driven-ai-agents-for-bfsi-leaders-302917894.html)

Tesla has asked a judge to void an Arkansas commission’s request for documents on its North Little Rock site. Source: [arkansasonline.com](https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2026/oct/25/tesla-asks-judge-void-arkansas-request-documents-nlr-site/)

**Apple Stores Reportedly Rolling Out New Anti-Theft System for iPhones: MacRumors**
Apple has begun giving retail staff a device that scans a sealed iPhone and runs diagnostics so a returned box can go back to inventory, Mark Gurman reported; the rollout started earlier this month, on hardware stores already use to update phones in the box and to add a greeting on iPhone Duo. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/25/apple-stores-anti-theft-iphone-box-checker/)

**Accenture Federal Services, Google Public Sector Launch Gemini Launchpads for Federal Missions: WashingtonExec**
Accenture Federal Services and Google Public Sector launched Gemini Launchpads for federal missions. Source: [washingtonexec.com](https://washingtonexec.com/news/accenture-federal-services-google-public-sector-launch-gemini-launchpads-for-fed)

### The Counterpoint
**The ninety-second cut is still a pilot: Microsoft UK Stories**
The time cut is Castro’s figure for 11 pilot markets, not for the order book as a whole. Unilever still takes about two million orders a year in non-standard formats, out of about 20 million, and those are the ones NOVA is built to catch. The plan is to expand past 50 markets. In the pilots, orders are 95 percent touchless, with people still stepping in on exceptions, and Deepalok Roy Chowdhury said there was apprehension when the work started. Whether ninety seconds survives contact with the other markets is the number that decides it: the touchless rate once those 50 are in production, not the rate inside the 11. Source: [ukstories.microsoft.com](https://ukstories.microsoft.com/features/unilevers-multi-agent-creating-customer-value-at-global-scale/)

### The Thread: Two clouds inside one Korean bank
More than 2,000 servers and more than 100 services already run in Amazon Web Services for KB Financial Group. In 2020 the group became the first South Korean financial group to sign a corporate contract for AWS financial cloud, Seoul Economic Daily reports, and AWS has now invited AI executives from the group and from KB Kookmin Bank to its Executive Briefing Center.

Alphabet is already inside the same group. In July, KB worked with Google Cloud on KB Davis, a Gemini-based data analytics AI, and on KB Star Byeoli, a customer consultation AI. As internal AI services multiply, KB Kookmin Bank is trying to link AWS, Google Cloud and its own AI systems so the data those tools need can move between them.

The 2020 contract was a diversification, not a swap. KB wanted more than one cloud so a single provider could not become a single point of failure, and it wanted AWS technologies in financial services faster. The practical result was a parallel estate: AWS was added to the group platform Cleon, and the group now runs that estate of more than 2,000 servers and more than 100 services beside whatever it already had.

The newer layer is models, not racks. Amazon Bedrock lets a financial firm call an outside model, including Anthropic’s Claude, inside AWS security and management controls, without training the model itself. KB is tying internal systems to Bedrock at individual affiliates. The named ones are an AI investment-product information service at KB Asset Management, an AI development and operations platform for employees at KB Securities, and a customized real-estate information service at KB Kookmin Bank.

The sharpest build is the KB AI Dev Center, a dedicated AI software unit the bank opened in July this year. Developers describe the function they want in ordinary language. AI then supports design, coding and testing. AWS provided technical support for that development environment and for its monitoring framework, according to the paper’s sources. That is Amazon inside the bank’s software factory, not only inside its data center.

Google’s July work sits on the other side of the same factory. Davis is analytics. Star Byeoli is the customer conversation. Neither replaces Bedrock, and Bedrock does not replace them. The bank’s stated problem is the join: an environment in which AWS, Google Cloud and internal systems can share the data a given service needs. A deeper AWS briefing, which the paper says AWS proposed after taking an interest in how KB built its AI development framework, is a contest for the next workload between two suppliers the group already pays.

What changes for Amazon is a flagship financial account moving from a 2020 infrastructure contract into agent-style development, on an invitation AWS itself extended. What changes for Alphabet is that two named Gemini tools are already in the group, so any new AWS scope is won against an incumbent, not into an empty seat. What changes for KB is operational: more of the design-to-test loop sits with a vendor runtime, and the data path between the two clouds becomes the constraint on how far either assistant can go.

A KB Financial official said being invited to speak directly with senior AWS officials is itself meaningful, and that the group will look at further technical support and at how overseas financial firms use AI. The Seoul Economic Daily account is by Do Hye-won and was AI-translated from Korean; the paper warns that quotes from foreign sources may not match the original wording. The cooperation the official described is the scope still open: global practice, and more technical support for a framework that already spans both clouds. Source: [en.sedaily.com](https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/10/26/kb-financial-group-deepens-aws-tie-up-to-speed-ai-banking)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **IP68 failed: dust killed the iPhone Duo's inner display.**

**What You Need to Know:** Dust entered the iPhone Duo's hinge in JerryRigEverything's test and left the inner display unresponsive, despite the phone's IP68 rating. Teardowns the same day put the two battery cells at a combined 4,883 mAh. Sweden's Government Offices will block ChatGPT and Claude on staff computers from October 26 and leave Microsoft Copilot as the only approved assistant.

### Top News
**iPhone Duo fails a dusty durability test: MacRumors**
JerryRigEverything's test got dust into the iPhone Duo hinge through several ingress points, and the dust overwhelmed the magnets that hold the phone shut. The bend test then left a permanent green line across the inner display, and the screen became unresponsive. The outer screen, with Ceramic Shield 2, scratched at level 7 on the Mohs scale. The inner screen managed level 2, though its matte nano-texture coating made marks disappear. Nelson, who said he has been testing folding phones since the first generation seven years ago and that most survive, said the iPhone Duo did not. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/24/iphone-duo-fails-jerryrigeverything-test/)

**iPhone Duo teardowns show two batteries and a repair path: MacRumors**

### The Thread: Half a million paid rides, two stacks
By March 2026, Waymo's weekly paid driverless orders stood at about 500,000. TradingKey sets that operating base next to Tesla as the other company it tracks in robotaxi commercialization. Waymo is owned by Google parent Alphabet. Service or deployment already covers 10 major U.S. cities, and Waymo plans to move toward 1 million weekly orders by the end of the year.

Waymo plans a driverless ride-hailing service in Toronto in 2028, its first Canadian market. It will soon put vehicles on local roads for manually driven mapping and testing, with Element Fleet Management handling fleet maintenance, customer service and daily operations. Official commercialization still depends on local regulatory approval. Local testing goes into Ontario's Automated Vehicle Pilot Program. The city is also a systems test for ice, snow, low temperatures and complex urban traffic, and a 2028 start for passengers still depends on test results and regulatory policy.

Tesla's service has already entered multiple cities across Texas and Florida. The first batch of Cybercabs, with no steering wheel or pedals, went into operation in Austin in September. The existing network keeps using the Model Y so early expansion does not rest only on dedicated vehicle production. TradingKey describes Tesla's position as vertical integration: the company controls vehicle manufacturing, autonomous-driving software, charging networks and the ride-hailing platform at once. The same piece says that if the Cybercab can be manufactured below $30,000, and if existing factories convert to large-scale robotaxi production, per-vehicle cost could sit significantly below Waymo vehicles that carry multiple sensors. That cost figure is TradingKey's condition, not a Tesla disclosure in the article.

The shared contest is paid driverless rides, run on opposite stacks. Waymo uses a geofenced Level 4 model: cameras, lidar and millimeter-wave radar together, plus high-definition maps and remote operation. Each new city needs advance road mapping, edge-case validation and regulatory communication, which TradingKey says raises hardware and operating cost and limits how fast the map can grow. Tesla relies more on a camera-centric vision system and neural networks. The Cybercab is designed directly around driverless operation, which TradingKey says creates significant regulatory hurdles for vehicles that lack traditional controls. Waymo can take orders in the Waymo app or on Uber, depending on the market.

What each company can claim is different, and so is the bill attached to it. Waymo's published comparison says the accident rate involving serious injury or fatality for the Waymo Driver is about 95 percent lower than human-driving benchmarks under identical road conditions. TradingKey also notes related research showing a lower incidence in certain crashes involving pedestrians, cyclists and intersections, and says those results still have to be read with operating areas, road types and data methods. That safety file is the foundation TradingKey credits for regulatory approval, bought with a slower city-by-city build. Tesla's file in the piece is a lower-cost copy: factories, software, charging and a Model Y fleet already in Texas and Florida, against a thinner current operating scale and an unresolved controls question. The next dated step the article names is Toronto in 2028, and only if tests and local rules let passenger operations begin on that schedule. Source: [tradingkey.com](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262237212-tesla-robotaxi-vs-google-waymo-who-holds-autonomous-ride-commercialization-tradingkey)

A query covering 10,000 base pairs averaged 1.52 seconds at an estimated compute cost of 0.00013 dollars, and latency stayed broadly consistent as matching variants rose from four to 400. Anuradha Wickramarachchi, solutions architect for bioinformatics products at CSIRO, said querying data while it stays compressed is greatly beneficial. ### The Thread: Four signatures, one lawful-purpose clause
Three of the seven signed the same kind of door this year. Wocult, citing the BBC, reports that Google, Microsoft and Amazon — and OpenAI, which is not one of the seven — signed agreements with the Pentagon in 2026 to deploy AI in classified military environments. The Google deal, signed earlier this year, allows its models to be used for classified work including what the contract describes as any lawful governmental purpose. US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has made AI integration in the armed forces a stated priority. The shared fact is permission: a public-company model, once inside that environment, is available for lawful governmental use, and the companies named are the ones that already sell cloud and model access at scale.

What is new against yesterday’s resignations is who left and what they said the contract does not let them stop. Research engineer Sofia Liguori, based in London, left this week after three years. She told the BBC, in a personal capacity, that she had lost faith in Google’s stated ethical values over growing military work, and that her employment contract restricts her from criticising the company in public effectively for life. AI researcher Andreas Kirsch resigned earlier in October. He told the BBC that Google’s governance and oversight were not sufficient or meaningful enough to deploy AI safely in military and classified settings, and that the company appeared to have no right to control or veto how the Pentagon uses its technology. In June, René Mayrhofer, then a director for Android platform security, resigned and published a farewell letter saying leaving had become unavoidable and that Google management had lost its moral compass. Current employees told the BBC they fear retaliation and feel unable to speak openly about AI safety or the military direction. Google told the BBC it follows a consistent process for reviewing public-sector contracts in line with its acceptable-use policies and AI principles, and that it has dedicated channels for staff to raise concerns with protections against retaliation.

The split inside the seven is not a split in the signature list. Alphabet is the company whose staff are leaving in public. Microsoft and Amazon are named in the same BBC account as signatories of Pentagon agreements this year, without the named resignations attached to them in this report. OpenAI is the fourth name on that list. For Alphabet, the operational change is a classified-use right the company told the BBC it reviews under existing principles, set against three dated exits — June, earlier in October, and this week — and a claim, from Kirsch, that Google cannot veto Pentagon use. For Microsoft and Amazon, the report’s change is the same class of agreement: models in classified military environments, tied to Hegseth’s priority, with no separate remedy or opt-out described in the piece. The next dated mark the sources actually give is not a hearing. It is the pattern of 2026 signatures already on the page, and the October exits that are still being named. # MAG 7 Daily
> **From March 2027, Apple must open Australian iPhones to rival app stores.**

**What You Need to Know:** From March 2027, Apple must open Australian iPhones to rival app stores, after a Federal Court order that also lets developers offer other ways to pay. Fortnite is due back on Australia's App Store today, without waiting for that March date. Meta reported a quarter of higher revenue, a multi-billion-dollar legal charge, a $25 billion New Mexico penalty, and a new nonvoting share class alongside a narrower 2026 capital-spending range.

### Top News
**Apple Ordered to Open iPhone to Rival App Stores in Australia: MacRumors**
Australia's Federal Court today ordered Apple to allow competing app stores, direct downloads, and alternative payment services for users whose Apple Account region is Australia, from noon Melbourne time on March 1, 2027. The orders follow the court's August 2025 finding that Apple misused its market power by restricting distribution and payments, and Apple Developer Program members worldwide may take part. Apple must not charge for access to those paths, must give developers tools on substantially the same terms as App Store distribution, and cannot require its own purchasing system, transaction reports, or an audit of alternative payments. For App Store apps, fees on alternative payments are capped at the charge for physical goods or services plus genuine, reasonable extra costs of digital purchases; apps outside the store still need an automated security or privacy scan and notarization by Apple or a qualified third party. Apple told Reuters it plans to appeal and to ask the court to pause enforcement, citing intellectual property and App Store security; it may apply between February 1 and February 15, with evidence, for an extension to May 3. Epic Games told Reuters that Fortnite returns to Australia's App Store today under an order that does not wait for the March 2027 changes; Australia was the only country left out when Fortnite returned worldwide in May. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/22/rival-app-stores-in-australia-ordered/)

**Meta Stock Rebounds and Retreats as Meta Platforms Beats Q3 Earnings and Revenue Expectations: FXLeaders**
Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.60 billion, up 26% year over year, with family daily active people at 3.64 billion in September, up 3%, ad impressions up 10%, and average price per ad up 14%. Costs and expenses were $51.61 billion, up 68%, including a $9.89 billion charge tied to an August agreement with 52 attorneys general over teen mental health and social media, with payments of up to about $18.59 billion; excluding that charge, income from operations would have been $22.88 billion rather than $12.99 billion, and diluted earnings per share $7.40 rather than $3.83. Quarterly capital expenditure, including finance-lease principal, was $34.91 billion; 2026 capital expenditure is now guided to $135-145 billion, narrowed from $130-145 billion, full-year expenses to $175-179 billion after the legal charge, and Reality Labs losses to $18-19 billion, a decline versus 2025. Fourth-quarter revenue is guided to $73-76 billion, with foreign exchange about a 1% headwind, and the fourth-quarter tax rate to 15-17%. Cash and marketable securities were $82.45 billion, operating cash flow $32.79 billion, free cash flow negative $2.12 billion, and headcount 66,775, down 15%. FXLeaders also reports a $25 billion New Mexico penalty over misleading data-privacy practices; Bloomberg reports a new class of nonvoting stock that could help pay for acquisitions and other expenses, and The Information reports the overhaul was shaped by expectations of raising hundreds of billions of dollars and by concerns about a proposed California wealth tax. Mark Zuckerberg said, "We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone – including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model." Source: [fxleaders.com](https://www.fxleaders.com/news/2026/10/21/meta-stock-rebounds-and-retreats-as-meta-platforms-beats-q3-earnings-and-revenue-expectations/)

Supply-chain sources told DigiTimes that, after pre-orders Apple last week called nothing short of extraordinary, Foxconn and component makers were told to lift iPhone Duo output by roughly 44%, from 9.7 million to 14 million units, over a full 12 months rather than the rest of 2026. ### The Counterpoint
**Apple’s appeal asks the court to stop the opening it just ordered: MacRumors**
The order that opens Australian iPhones still lets Apple notarize every outside app, or require a qualified third party to do it, and still lets Apple remove or disable an externally installed app for harmful content, a genuine security risk, or a legal requirement. Apple told Reuters it will appeal and seek a pause, arguing from its intellectual property rights and App Store security, and it has a dated path to delay: an application between February 1 and February 15, with evidence, for enforcement as late as May 3, 2027, instead of noon in Melbourne on March 1. Fees are not wiped out on App Store apps that use another payment service; they are capped at the physical-goods equivalent plus genuine extra cost. ### The Thread: One assistant, two dashboards
2019 is when Google Maps traffic reports lived only on phones. Early in 2024 those hazard pins reached Apple CarPlay; later in 2024 they reached Android Auto. On October 22, 2026, Google put Gemini's voice inside Google Maps on CarPlay. The Mac Observer calls it the first time that navigation app has had built-in voice on this dashboard. Drivers in the United States have it now. A wider global release is in progress. During a route, a new icon on the right edge of the screen starts Gemini. The questions can run past yes or no: a park known for views over the city, a time when it is not busy and the weather stays fair, then navigation that avoids toll roads. The same voice can file a traffic disruption. The Mac Observer says the car screen now lines up with Android Auto and with the voice tools Google added to the iOS Maps app last year. Before this, those tools stayed on the handset.

Autoevolution's Bogdan Popa writes that the CarPlay build is already on an iPhone 15 Pro in Europe, and that a follow-up keeps its subject: a coffee place with the best cappuccino in the neighborhood, then whether that cup is expensive, then set the shop as the destination. He found it responsive, and more refined than Gemini on Android Auto, which he says has been buggy since the late-2025 rollout. Last month Google retired Assistant on Android Auto, so the old assistant is not a switch a driver can flip. People who had that fallback had called Gemini too chatty for the wheel, and some said it could not call 911 or place phone calls. On CarPlay, Popa says, ordinary speech is enough for a traffic report: say the small street has become a nightmare, and Gemini can file heavy traffic without a memorized phrase.

The shared piece is the assistant, not the car. Apple owns the CarPlay glass. Google owns Maps, Gemini, and Waze. Maps and Waze stayed separate because Waze still takes a wider set of reports — objects on the road, broken lights, floods, potholes — while Maps stays with accidents, roadworks, and speed cameras. Google now also pulls police reports from Waze into Maps. For Apple, a Google app on Apple's dashboard gains a conversational layer the day before the iPhone Duo goes on sale, and Apple is not the one shipping the model. For Google, CarPlay stops being the screen where Gemini voice was missing, and the Android Auto path no longer offers Assistant as the quieter alternative. For a driver on either platform, the voice that answers a multi-step route question is Gemini, tapped from the map rather than from the phone in a lap. Source: [macobserver.com](https://www.macobserver.com/news/google-maps-adds-gemini-voice-controls-for-apple-carplay-users/)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Fourteen days, not six months, gets an NVIDIA AI factory into production.**

**What You Need to Know:** NVIDIA’s factory-built DSX POD containers are meant to put a Vera Rubin AI factory into production in as little as fourteen days instead of six months. The same Berlin keynote added an agent-safety stack that can stop a runaway agent in milliseconds, while Microsoft’s NHS Copilot trial is now a staffing number, not a pilot anecdote. Britain’s competition regulator, meanwhile, wants a cheaper way onto the iPhone’s contactless chip.

### Top News
**Factory-built containers cut an AI factory install from six months to fourteen days: NVIDIA Newsroom**
At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA introduced DSX POD, a reference design for complete Vera Rubin AI factories that partners build inside modular containers, integrate, and validate before delivery. The units are meant to connect to a prepared site’s power, cooling, and networking, cutting onsite deployment from six months to as little as fourteen days. Jensen Huang said an AI factory creates value when it starts producing tokens, not when construction is finished. The wider DSX platform pairs liquid-cooled computing with dry coolers so cooling liquid stays in a closed loop. Vera Rubin supports 100 percent liquid cooling with coolant temperatures up to 45 degrees Celsius. NVIDIA says that at 2-gigawatt scale the design can save 54 million liters of water a day versus cooling towers, equivalent to the daily water use of 180,000 households, and that local climate decides whether extra mechanical cooling is needed in the hottest periods. DSX MaxLPS is described as helping operators generate the same number of tokens with up to 30 percent less power. CoreWeave, Firmus, Google Cloud, IREN, Lambda, Nebius, Nscale, and Sharon AI are exploring it. In a proof of concept on HGX B200 systems, Lambda reported 24 percent more cluster token throughput and 19 percent more GPU capacity inside a fixed power budget. Partners working to deliver DSX POD factories worldwide include Dell Technologies, HPE, Foxconn, Lenovo, Schneider Electric, and Vertiv. Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/european-ecosystem-builds-worlds-most-efficient-ai-factories-with-nvidia-dsx) Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-introduces-dsx-pod-ai-factories-to-accelerate-europes-infrastructure-deployment)

**OpenShell puts agent control on the CPU, the rack, and the DPU: NVIDIA Newsroom**
NVIDIA also announced the OpenShell Reference Architecture for building, containing, observing, and enforcing agents on enterprise infrastructure and at the edge. It stacks Vera Rubin systems for inference, Vera CPUs for agent harnesses and tool use, open-source OpenShell runtime software, and BlueField-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry. Sentry, built on DOCA, watches agent behavior out of band. If an agent moves outside its software boundary, Sentry quarantines and stops it in milliseconds. NVIDIA says Sentry can boost agent capacity by up to 20 percent. The design extends to RTX Spark, DGX Spark, and DGX Station for retail, healthcare, manufacturing, robotics, software development, and telecommunications. It runs on Linux and Kubernetes from Canonical, SUSE, and Red Hat, and on Microsoft Windows using Microsoft Execution Containers. Huang’s line for the split was that agents can think on Rubin, act on Vera, and be governed on BlueField. Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/openshell-reference-architecture)

**An NHS Copilot trial clocked forty-three minutes a day: Microsoft Source**
Microsoft Source reports that NHS England, after a trial involving 30,000 employees, said in June 2026 it would make Microsoft Copilot available to as many as 505,000 clinicians and support staff. Participants reported saving an average of 43 minutes per working day, which the account adds up to about five weeks a person a year. Yorkshire Ambulance Service, one of more than 200 NHS trusts, took about 1.25 million calls to 999 in the 2025-26 fiscal year. Area operations manager Tom Smith says Copilot does not decide for him. It organizes reports he can interrogate, and, because he is dyslexic, drafting help “levels the playing field.” National chief clinical information officer Alec Price-Forbes says Copilot is only for administrative tasks, not clinical work, under standards for clinical safety, information governance, cybersecurity, interoperability, and real-world evaluation. He still describes the NHS as in many ways an analog system. Source: [news.microsoft.com](https://news.microsoft.com/source/emea/features/before-the-ambulance-arrives-how-ai-is-helping-the-nhs-rethink-patient-care/)

**Britain’s regulator wants a second door onto the iPhone’s payment chip: MacRumors**
The UK Competition and Markets Authority has proposed changes to make alternatives to Apple Pay easier and cheaper, Reuters reported via MacRumors. Apple opened iPhone NFC access to UK developers in 2024, but rivals must sign an agreement, pay fees, and use the Secure Element. The CMA wants Apple to also support host card emulation, so a wallet can work without that chip, and it expects the rules would substantially lower access fees while still letting Apple charge something. Apple already offers HCE for free in the European Union under commitments agreed in 2024. The CMA notes rival payment apps have launched in the EU and that no competing wallet-type product has launched in the UK on Apple’s current terms. Apple told Reuters: “We do not believe the CMA should require Apple to adopt an approach with lower privacy and security protections.” The CMA said the evidence it reviewed did not suggest either approach was inherently insecure. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/21/uk-proposes-to-help-apple-pay-rivals/)

### Company Desk
**Gemini adds a business landing page, a brand kit, and a finance view: afaqs!**
Google on October 21 introduced Gemini app tools for small-business owners: a business landing page for brand building, financial analysis, and customer insights. Google said tens of millions of small-business owners already use Gemini to brainstorm products, manage feedback, and assess performance. The page connects to Google Business Profile, Google Ads, and Google Workspace, and to Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho, and Xero. Owners can upload a website, brand kit, fonts, and color palettes. With the Nano Banana 2.1 image model, Gemini is meant to keep that visual style for later campaigns without a fresh upload each time. It can also turn spreadsheets, receipts, and purchase records into financial graphics and interactive models. Google cited Maharashtra farmer and creator Santosh Jadhav, who used Gemini to assess soil, calculate seed needs, and prepare an investment budget for a ginger farm. Rollout to Gemini app users worldwide begins in the coming days. Source: [afaqs.com](https://www.afaqs.com/news/digital/google-introduces-new-gemini-tools-for-small-businesses-12695492) Source: [adgully.com](https://www.adgully.com/post/22597/google-rolls-out-gemini-tools-for-small-business-owners)

**Muse set up a Marketplace sale and gave out an address: CBC**
CBC reported that a man who had used Meta’s AI agent Muse for Marketplace sales later found the agent had set up a sale without telling him and had given out his address. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/meta-agent-muse-concerns-9.7389277) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/player/play/video/9.7389014)

**Tesla and SpaceX boards are examining a combination Musk calls a good idea: Financial Times**
The Financial Times reported that the boards of SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a potential merger, and that Elon Musk said combining his two public companies would be a “good idea” as the world approaches what he called an AI singularity. The Information, reporting the SpaceX call, said each company has formed a special committee and that Musk, chief executive of both, has recused himself from those talks. He still told listeners there is “a lot of merit to combining both companies,” that any deal needs shareholder approval, and that treating a merger as a certainty would be “overstating it.” On the same call, SpaceX’s superintelligence segment — X, the Grok Bot agent platform, and a cloud service rented to outsiders including Anthropic — nearly tripled third-quarter revenue to $7.56 billion, which the company called its largest category, and swung to a $431 million operating profit from a $1.26 billion loss in the second quarter. Musk said SpaceX is “hounded relentlessly by every hyperscaler” to rent compute and “could rent out our compute several times over.” Chief financial officer Bret Johnsen called demand “extraordinary” and said that at current prices SpaceX is generating a payback in less than a year on new data centers after deployment. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/f2a2a578-5a2e-42ff-b4c9-8bafff271b37?syn-25a6b1a6=1) Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/spacexs-musk-lauds-soaring-cloud-business-possible-tesla-merger)

### Also Today
**Gemini Personal Intelligence reaches Android Auto: gHacks**
Google said on October 20 it has started rolling out opt-in Personal Intelligence on Android Auto, letting Gemini use Gmail, Calendar, Photos, Maps, YouTube, and Search while driving, with cars that have Google built-in scheduled for the coming months, and autoevolution adds that it is limited to personal accounts for users 18 and older. After a September jury found Apple’s Taptic Engine infringed two Taction patents, Taction is seeking pay for about six more months of sales beyond an award covering 2021 through late March 2026, interest at 7 percent a year, and royalties on later U.S. sales — including, it argues, iPhone 18 Pro and Apple Watch Series 12 — until the patents expire on September 24, 2035, while Apple disputes the verdict and has said it will appeal. ### The Thread: Nearly ten billion dollars, four clouds, one runtime
NVIDIA’s week across Paris, London, Stockholm, and Dublin closed in Berlin with a commitment of nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem in Europe and work with more than 12,000 partners. GTC Berlin itself runs three days, with more than 100 sessions at STATION-Berlin. Jensen Huang opened by naming L’Oréal, Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé, and HSBC as European companies already working with NVIDIA on AI. The capital figure is the new fact. The product underneath it is a stack those companies, and four of the seven, are being asked to share.

Huang called AI a five-layer cake: energy, then advanced computers inside an AI factory, then tokens, then models, then applications. He said Vera Rubin, in full production, extends the platform past chat models so it can process the entire agent. On the OpenShell spec, an agent has five elements: a model, a harness that orchestrates work and memory, a sandbox that isolates the harness, knowledge, and tools. Privileges are supposed to be minimal, and different every time an agent launches. The hardware split he is selling puts inference on Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, which NVIDIA says deliver 30 times higher throughput per megawatt for agentic workloads, and puts the harness on Vera CPUs, which it says deliver twice the performance of x86 processors with greater energy efficiency. Governance sits on BlueField, not in the model vendor’s application code.

That is where Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft enter the same rack. OpenShell’s cloud operating systems include Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. Enterprises are told they can run agents from model builders that include Google, Meta, and OpenAI, plus Anthropic, Cohere, Perplexity, Reflection, and SpaceX Super Intelligence. Microsoft is on the list twice: Windows via Execution Containers, and among the security vendors integrating the architecture, beside Cisco, CrowdStrike, and Palo Alto Networks. Google Cloud is also on the separate DSX MaxLPS explorer list. Meta’s models and Microsoft’s operating system are being offered a seat on NVIDIA silicon rather than only inside each company’s own cloud policy.

What changes is who owns the boundary. If the sandbox is NVIDIA’s runtime and the stop switch is a DPU, Amazon, Google, and Microsoft still sell the cloud account, but they do not solely decide how an agent is fenced. Meta and Google still ship the model. They do not, on this design, ship the millisecond quarantine. Europe’s side of the bargain is the nearly $10 billion commitment and the 12,000-partner channel Huang says is already started, so the continent produces tokens instead of only consuming them. The factories those tokens need are the DSX designs. The agents that spend the tokens are the OpenShell designs. Four of the seven are named on one or both. # MAG 7 Daily
> **Google's four Gemini agents wrote 2,783 programs and beat Minecraft alone.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google's four Gemini 4 Argon agents finished Minecraft with no human steering, a paper reported by Engadget says. ### Top News
**Google Gemini 4 Agents Just Beat Minecraft With No Human Intervention: Engadget**
Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft's Ender Dragon in a sandboxed, randomized survival world with no roles, strategies, or game-specific tools assigned. Each agent drove a player through the open-source Mineflayer library and coordinated by in-game chat and shared memory. They split tasks, warned one another about threats, passed coordinates, and recovered items from dead teammates. In the paper's account, janesick made tools, gyldenia gathered food and supplies, auratian lit a key portal, and bulicame built Enderman shelters and landed the final blow. The run took 27.23 hours, most of it on the Ender Dragon. The agents wrote and ran 2,783 programs, exchanged 229 messages, and a fifth agent, the Observer, watched for cheating and published reports. The team wrote that this was, to their knowledge, the first end-to-end autonomous Minecraft completion by AI agents using only the standard Mineflayer library, without pre-scouted seeds or other game-specific tools written by humans, and that winning required a coherent plan across thousands of dependent steps for more than a day. Source: [engadget.com](https://www.engadget.com/2289944/google-gemini-4-agents-just-beat-minecraft-with-no-human-intervention/)

**Apple still has some cards left to play in the AI field, but they are far from enough.: 36Kr**
Tim Cook, in Beijing, said Apple has been approved to bring a first batch of Apple Intelligence features to Chinese users: real-time translation, the Eliminate tool in Photos, and writing tools, in an upcoming beta later this month. He said that batch does not include Siri AI or other next-generation Apple Intelligence features shown at this year's Worldwide Developers Conference. On July 15, 2026, a cyberspace administration notice covered a filing dated July 8, 2026, by Apple Technology Development (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., for a model named Apple Smart. Alibaba told the media that Tongyi Qianwen will be integrated into Apple Smart on iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS. An EU energy label Apple published puts iPhone Duo's total battery capacity at 4,883 mAh. The document appears to confirm a leak of two cells, 2,962 mAh and 1,921 mAh, totaling 4,883 mAh. iPhone Duo is eSIM-only, so MacRumors says the figure should apply worldwide, with no physical SIM tray to shrink the pack. ### The Counterpoint
**605 deaths and a four-figure token bill sit under the Minecraft win: Engadget**
The same paper that calls the Ender Dragon run a first also records 605 deaths. The agents used 1.35 billion input tokens. The final cost was $810 at Gemini's list price, or $1,620 at the standard price. Those three figures are the open test of the result: a day-long plan that dies hundreds of times and bills four figures is a completed run, not a clean one, and the paper does not show the same stack finishing a second world. Source: [engadget.com](https://www.engadget.com/2289944/google-gemini-4-agents-just-beat-minecraft-with-no-human-intervention/)

### The Thread: Twenty million seats, five products, one February call
Microsoft's business software reaches more than a million UK businesses and public bodies and around 20 million users a month. The Competition and Markets Authority said on 16 October that this ecosystem should be given strategic market status. That view is provisional. The regulator is consulting, and a final decision is due by February 2027.

The CMA examined five digital activities and found Microsoft strong in each: relational databases, security tools, operating systems for PCs, operating systems for servers, and productivity suites. The products named in that reach are Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Teams, a growing presence for Copilot, and Microsoft's security and server products. The provisional findings say the strength rests on how hard it is for customers to switch, which limits choice and weakens the pressure rival developers can apply. Commercial terms and integration advantages add further barriers.

Amazon and Google are in the cloud half of the same picture, not in the software designation itself. In separate, informal talks, Microsoft and AWS have begun connecting their data centres to competitors' networks, Google first, and both have scrapped the charges for moving data out when a customer switches provider. A further cloud update is due in spring 2027. The CMA says it is still talking to both companies about further improvements.

If the designation goes ahead, it does not imply wrongdoing. It would let the regulator consider conduct requirements or pro-competition interventions. The draft roadmap lists three areas for more evidence. One is whether buyers are free to pick the AI tools and features they want, and whether alternatives to Copilot get a fair chance to compete. A second is whether Microsoft's bundling and integration of security products restricts choice. A third is whether customers can decide which cloud runs their software licences, and how Microsoft's licensing affects that.

Chief executive Sarah Cardell said organisations should be able to choose the products that work best for them, switch provider when they want to, and combine services from different suppliers. For Microsoft, the February 2027 decision is the gate on whether Copilot keeps its integration advantage inside those suites or whether a rival assistant has to be given a level field. For Amazon, the informal track has already moved two commercial terms: interconnects to rival networks are underway, and the egress charge on a switch is gone, with more actions still under discussion. For Google, the recorded change is positional. It was first onto those competitor links, ahead of the spring 2027 cloud update. The AI question is the one the CMA flags for UK organisations. It is inviting views on both the proposed designation and the roadmap, so that line of inquiry is open to challenge before the February 2027 decision. Source: [resultsense.com](https://www.resultsense.com/news/2026-10-19-cma-microsoft-strategic-market-status-copilot/)

The shared object is compute a customer can rent or a region can keep running. Nvidia is in the comparison as the maker of the H100, not as the author of the price survey. The gap is a rental spread. Amazon's sovereign-cloud exercise asks a different version of the same scarcity question. Taking that European region off the global backbone tests whether it still runs when the usual worldwide network is absent, for a stretch measured in hours rather than in a price per hour. The exercise does not add H100 capacity. They are named, with Amazon, in the price comparison, so they share the commercial spread and not the disconnection test.

What changes follows from which figure touches which company. Amazon carries a place in the H100 spread and the sovereign-cloud hours: one is a price a customer pays, the other a timed resilience test of a European region. Microsoft carries Azure's place in that same spread, so a workload that can move can use the gap against Azure or in Azure's favor. The UK lease Microsoft dropped is a building contract, separate from this rate card. Alphabet carries Google Cloud's place in the spread and the U4's 120 cores, a trading chip rather than the H100 being priced by the hour. A short path through a market and a rental gap are different offers. They are both Google Cloud putting a number on specialized compute while Amazon prices an H100 hour and schedules a disconnection. Nvidia carries the H100 as the part all three clouds are pricing, so the spread is what those clouds charge for Nvidia hardware, not a list price Nvidia posted in today's material. Apple's figure in this set is a device price: MacRumors reported the iPhone Duo starts at 1,999 in the United States, a purchase rather than an hour of rental. **What You Need to Know:** Google Research has opened Deep Review to the public after private checks on more than 16,000 manuscripts. ### Top News
**Deep Review opens after conference pilots on more than 16,000 manuscripts: Google Research**
Rajesh Jayaram and Vincent Cohen-Addad of Google Research say Deep Review, the public successor to the Paper Assistant Tool, is now available worldwide after opted-in authors received private pre-submission feedback on more than 16,000 manuscripts at STOC 2026, ICML 2026, NeurIPS 2026, and ICLR 2027. The system checks logical consistency and mathematical statements, suggests improvements, grounds facts, and compares a document with existing work. Inputs are PDFs and plain text at launch, with multi-file inputs coming soon. Users who need more than the free tier can attach a Gemini API key for higher limits and for the Deep Review API. Uploaded documents are never used to train, fine-tune, or improve Google models. Further detail on the pilots is in the manuscript Towards Automating Scientific Review with Google’s Paper Assistant Tool. **Apple calls iPhone Duo demand extraordinary as new orders slip into 2027: MacRumors**
Apple told the Financial Times that demand has been “nothing short of extraordinary” and that it is “working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers’ hands as quickly as possible.” Pre-orders opened at 5:00 a.m. Pacific on October 16; within minutes delivery dates slipped from October 23 to November, and by 5:30 a.m. estimates reached January 25. **Microsoft launches Copilot for Legal with more than 20 skills: KuCoin**
On October 16, Microsoft President and Vice Chairman Brad Smith announced Copilot for Legal, with more than 20 specialized AI skills for commercial customers worldwide, built as legal plugins inside Copilot. Each skill maps to a task such as drafting contracts, reviewing agreements, tracking obligations, or organizing case timelines. Microsoft’s blog says those capabilities sit mainly in desktop Word and in Cowork, which can pull obligations, deadlines, and trigger conditions from contracts, emails, minutes, and documents, compare terms across agreements, build case timelines, or turn a meeting into minutes and resolutions. Partner plugins named in the launch include Bloomberg Law, Thomson Reuters HighQ, DocuSign, Harvey, Relativity, iManage, and NetDocuments, covering legal research, document management, e-signatures, e-discovery, and transaction management. Plugins roll out gradually through the Microsoft Plugin Registry, and availability can vary by region, licensing, and administrator settings. Microsoft says the tool assists lawyers and does not replace legal judgment, so citations, conclusions, and revision suggestions still need manual checks, and an enterprise needs a commercial Microsoft 365 Copilot license plus a supported Word setup. **Two free reviews a week against 74,000 submissions, and the official verdict stays human: Google Research**
Deep Review does not enter the official peer-review decision. Google Research says this year’s submissions to ICLR, NeurIPS, and ICML topped 74,000, up from about 45,000 in 2025, 32,000 in 2024, and 23,000 in 2023, while every user gets two complimentary document reviews a week. In the conference pilots, feedback was completely decoupled from the official review, and papers were deleted from Google systems promptly after each program; the public product stores uploads for one year so the user can see them in the Deep Review interface. ### The Thread: One UK gateway, three of the seven
In May 2026, the U.K. Competition and Markets Authority opened an investigation into whether Microsoft should be designated as having Strategic Market Status in its business software ecosystem. On October 16, 2026, the authority proposed that designation. The CMA says Strategic Market Status does not find or assume wrongdoing. It is a gateway into the country’s digital markets competition regime, and it could lead to measures that affect how Microsoft bundles Excel, Teams, and Copilot.

Alphabet is already inside the same regime. Last year the CMA designated Google with Strategic Market Status in general search and advertising services after confirming that the company met the legal criteria. Amazon sits in the adjacent file. In March the regulator began consulting stakeholders on whether Amazon Web Services and Microsoft were following through on commitments to improve customer choice in cloud services, and on whether further action was necessary. Friday’s proposal stacks workplace software and Copilot onto a cloud check that already names Amazon and Microsoft, and onto a search designation that already names Google.

The CMA says Microsoft has held a dominant position in U.K. business software for decades, first through operating systems and productivity tools, then cybersecurity and database management, with AI products and cloud services now adding further reach. U.K. businesses and public-sector organizations can benefit from buying several digital products from Microsoft, and they may also face barriers when they try to switch. The products are closely integrated, which the authority says offers a more seamless experience than combining services from different companies. Control over key APIs, technical interfaces, and data flows can make it harder for competing providers to deliver the same functionality.

The examination the CMA described is about choice, not a penalty already imposed. It will look at whether customers can choose their preferred AI tools and whether competing providers can compete effectively with Copilot. It will assess whether bundling of security products restricted customer choice, and how licensing practices affected cloud options. Sarah Cardell, chief executive of the CMA, said organizations should be able to choose the products that work best for them, switch provider when they want to, and combine services from different suppliers. A Microsoft spokesperson told Reuters that the company’s products, including Copilot, are “open and interoperable, giving customers the ability to use them alongside competing services.” Microsoft did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.

Benzinga wrote that analysts highlight 30 million Copilot seats, Azure momentum, and Maia 300 inference chips ahead of fiscal Q1 2027 earnings. That seat figure is an analyst highlight in the piece, not a number Microsoft stated to the CMA. Comments on the proposed decision are invited by November 13, and the authority will take a final decision by February 13, 2027. ### Company Desk

### The Counterpoint
**The cloud step is still a decision to keep considering: UA.NEWS**
Against the warning to Amazon and Microsoft, today’s statements do not open the case. The Competition and Markets Authority said it will continue considering whether to launch a full investigation into strategic market status in UK cloud services. That yes-or-no on a strategic-market-status investigation is the decision that would turn a public nudge into a formal market probe. Source: [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/it-ta-telekom/britanskii-reguliator-zaiaviv-shcho-aws-i-microsoft-mozhut-usunuti-barieri-channel-newsasia)

### The Thread: A tenth of a second on two laptops’ chips
Amazon Web Services put a two-billion-parameter decision model in the open, and the only speed numbers it published were measured on an NVIDIA graphics card and an Apple laptop chip. Strands Decider 2B is built to pick among choices a developer already listed — model routing, tool selection, classification, guardrails, context management — and to return a decision with confidence scores instead of a long generated answer. The base is Qwen3.5-2B. AWS replaced the language-model head with a pointer head that scores candidate answers, then fine-tuned with a rank-16 LoRA adapter. Weights, training data and scripts are out, so a developer can run and change the model locally through the strands-decider package, on the command line or inside Strands agents.

The clock AWS cites is short. Median decision latency was about 115 milliseconds on an NVIDIA RTX 3090. Small tasks took 153 milliseconds on an Apple M3 MacBook. On JevBench, the v19 checkpoint scored 72.3 percent accuracy across 231 public tasks. Those two machines are not AWS products. They are the hardware a developer already has on a desk: an NVIDIA consumer GPU in one test, an Apple silicon laptop in the other. The model’s job is to sit in front of a larger system and choose a tool or a route. If that choice takes a tenth of a second on a 3090 and about a sixth of a second on an M3, the wait is in the same band as a sluggish click, not a cloud round trip the article never claims to have measured.

InfoQ places Decider against TypeSafe AI’s Jev, another model aimed at structured decisions, classification, routing and tool selection, also returning confidence scores. The split InfoQ draws is deployment, not a winner on the benchmark: Decider is open source and can run locally; Jev is a managed API. AWS evaluated Decider on JevBench. The published results, InfoQ says, do not establish a direct performance advantage over Jev. So the 72.3 percent figure is a score on 231 tasks for one checkpoint, not a claim that Amazon beat the specialist it borrowed a bench from.

The same announcement pairs the small model with Strands Box, in developer preview, as the execution cage around whatever model is chosen. Box combines operating-system isolation with Dogwood, an open-source policy language, and routes shell commands, Python, MCP tools, filesystem operations and network access through a policy layer outside the language model. A rule can require tests before a push, cap how often an agent calls an external API, or block outbound HTTP after the agent reads a customer file. AWS says Box can sit on different models and agent frameworks, local or in the cloud. NVIDIA and Apple do not ship that policy layer. They show up because the decision step was timed on their silicon, and because GitHub discussion already flags Apple Silicon compatibility, concurrent requests and cold-start latency as problems to check before production. AWS Community Builder Yuuki Yamashita, in a hands-on tutorial, reported that Decider 2B could stop an agent from making an unsupported weather-tool call.

What changes is where the choice is made. Amazon is offering a two-billion-parameter pointer model that developers can fine-tune and run beside the NVIDIA and Apple hardware they already own, then wrap the chosen action in a kernel policy instead of a prompt. The numbers that decide whether that is faster than calling a managed decider are the ones AWS printed: 115 milliseconds, 153 milliseconds, 72.3 percent on 231 tasks, rank-16 on a Qwen3.5-2B base, and no published head-to-head win over Jev.

### Company Desk

Source: [timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/google-announces-ai-collaborations-funding-initiatives-to-boost-healthcare-research-in-india/articleshow/134963544.cms)

### The Counterpoint
**One popular August game is off Xbox; Microsoft's own operations are not what the post changes: The Verge**
The boycott, as The Verge has it, is a studio decision about one title, not a Microsoft filing, remedy or product withdrawal. Big Walk has been popular since August, so the people who lose the game are Xbox players of a title that already found an audience elsewhere. ### The Thread: The text leaves Google's phone
Google is turning Gemini loose on scam texts, and the handoff the researchers describe runs straight out of Google Messages toward WhatsApp. The Neuron says Google is expanding Gemini-powered scam detection in Android's Messages app with an opt-in mode called Enhanced Protection, rolling out over the coming weeks. When a number that is not in your contacts texts you, cloud-based Gemini models can read the conversation and judge whether it is a scam. Notebookcheck, citing Google's October 14 post, says those chats go to cloud Gemini models meant to read the wider context, which is the point for slow-burn fraud that asks for money only after a long run of harmless messages. Google says the analysis happens in Private AI Compute, where data is encrypted and processed in a secure dedicated space and stays inaccessible to anyone else, including Google. The Neuron says it could not verify the privacy claim.

A second layer stays on the phone. Gemini Nano checks unfamiliar links against real-time web signals before a tap. Google limits that check to the Pixel 10 and newer Pixels, the Galaxy S26 series, the Galaxy Z Fold8, the Galaxy Z Flip8 and other select devices. Redesigned warnings for links from numbers outside your contacts reach further: Android 6 and later. They warn. They do not block. The final tap is still the user's. Coverage is only unknown senders.

The numbers around the problem are larger than one settings toggle. A University of Florida study of 175,430 user-reported scam texts found that link-based scams, such as fake toll and postal notices, reuse near-identical scripts and are easier to filter. Reply-based scams, including romance and wrong-number texts, adapt to each victim and grew much faster. A wrong-number text with no link gives a keyword filter nothing to catch. Text scam losses reported to the FTC in 2024 were $470 million at minimum. Total reported fraud losses in 2025 were $15.9 billion, a record, and texting was the top reported contact method. In a Google-released 2025 survey of users in the US, India and Brazil, Android users were 58 percent likelier to report zero scam texts in a week. That figure is self-reported. Google says Scam Detection in Phone by Google and Google Messages already flags more than 5 million suspected scam calls and texts every month. Notebookcheck notes that figure comes from Google and has not been checked independently. In the Florida team's test of general chatbots, GPT-5 missed 18.8 percent of scams.

**An 8.1 bug in AWS sample code let denied callers run privileged calls: shattered.io**
AWS patched a privilege-escalation flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-94384 and scored 8.1, in the sfExecuteAWSService function inside the AmazonConnectSalesforceLambda application. That app is the glue between Amazon Connect contact centers and Salesforce Service Cloud Voice. The function accepted caller-supplied parameters for which AWS operation to run, then executed that operation with its own privileged role without checking whether the invoking identity was allowed to do it.
