# MAG 7 Daily
> **One unpatched key lets local Mac software hijack Meta's Muse assistant.**

**What You Need to Know:** One unpatched key lets local Mac software hijack Meta's Muse assistant, and the desktop client will send dictation audio plus the account token to whatever server that key names. SandboxAQ's potency model is now on the AWS Marketplace for North American commercial customers, and Meta-backed Eliyan is drawing takeover interest over AI data-transfer bottlenecks. Google is testing a Gemini 4 coding checkpoint called Carbon on an internal platform.

### Top News
**Unpatched Muse key lets local Mac software redirect dictation: 36Kr**
Patrick Wardle, founder of the Objective-See Foundation, has disclosed an unpatched flaw in Meta's new Muse macOS client, 36Kr reports. Software running as an ordinary user can overwrite an undocumented preference, endo_voyager_dictation_endpoint, without an administrator password or a macOS authorization prompt. That key names the server that receives dictation audio and returns the transcript. Change it, and the client sends raw microphone audio and the Muse account's authentication token to an endpoint the attacker controls. Wardle ran a proxy that forwarded traffic on to Meta while keeping the token and the audio. With the session, hidden instructions can be added to voice requests so the assistant acts in the background, including taking local documents or WhatsApp message records. Mark Zuckerberg had said the assistant was built with privacy and security at its core from the start. Source: [eu.36kr.com](https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/4019730918363011)

**SandboxAQ's AQPotency opens on the AWS Marketplace: Quantum Zeitgeist**
SandboxAQ's AQPotency is available to AWS commercial customers in North America through the AWS Marketplace, and it deploys as an Amazon SageMaker model package. It predicts how strongly a candidate compound binds a protein from a UniProt ID and a ligand SMILES string, with no 3D crystal structure, which brings in targets such as membrane proteins, mutant panels, and proteins that have not been crystallized. Teams can rank millions of compounds in a few hours on standard CPU instances inside their own AWS environment, through a real-time endpoint or large asynchronous jobs. SandboxAQ says it collects no metadata on users' targets or molecules. The model has also been reachable through Claude via the Model Context Protocol since August. Source: [quantumzeitgeist.com](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/aqpotency-available-aws-customers-north/)

**Meta-backed Eliyan draws takeover interest over AI data links: The Information**
Eliyan, backed by AMD, Cisco, and Meta, is drawing takeover interest, The Information reports. The interest is tied to data-transfer bottlenecks that are slowing AI systems. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/newsletters/dealmaker/networking-startup-eliyan-draws-takeover-interest-held-early-talks-arm?utm_campaign=Editorial&utm_content=Article&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_source=bluesky,threads,twitter)

**Google tests Gemini 4 Carbon on internal coding: The Decoder**
Google has put a Gemini 4 checkpoint called Carbon on its internal coding platform Jetski over the past few days, where it is said to beat still-unshipped Argon mainly on programming tasks, The Decoder reports from documents, screenshots, and internal chats Business Insider reviewed. One employee compared Carbon to Anthropic's Opus 5.5 and said it still needs more testing; early Argon builds reminded another employee of the older Opus 5 on some coding tasks. Google's own map calls Argon the frontier reasoning model, Flash the speed-and-volume model, Omni the generative-media model, and Gemma the lightweight open-weights edge model. Carbon and Barium read as checkpoints inside the Argon family: an employee called Carbon "Gemini pro next model," and internal documents had labeled the now-unveiled Argon as "Barium-B." DeepMind's Vedant Misra replied on X, "Have you heard of recursive self improvement." There is still no official Gemini 4 launch date. Logan Kilpatrick has confirmed the team is working on getting the most out of Argon. Source: [the-decoder.com](https://the-decoder.com/googles-gemini-4-carbon-model-is-reportedly-matching-anthropics-opus-5-5-coding-performance/)

### The Counterpoint
**The Muse hijack still needs software already on the Mac, and dictation switched on: 36Kr**
Wardle's path is not a remote break-in by itself. The rewrite is open to unprivileged local processes and arbitrary scripts already running as the user, and the microphone audio and token leave only when dictation is enabled. Meta has not issued a security advisory, the flaw has no CVE ID, and the open question is whether that preference stays writable before a patch lands. Source: [eu.36kr.com](https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/4019730918363011)

### The Thread: Three home platforms, seven bulbs
A roundup of seven smart bulbs treats Alexa, Google Home, and Apple Home as the test a lamp has to pass. Geeky Gadgets, drawing on a Smart Home 101 breakdown, highlights the ABRA bulb at a color rendering index of 90, with tunable white from 2700K to 6500K. ABRA comes as an A19 rated at 800 lumens and a BR30 rated at 750 lumens, and the write-up says it works with Alexa, Google Home, and Siri without a hub. LIFX is the brightness and wide-color option, also hub-free. Philips Hue is the customization lane: Chroma Sync, plus an optional Hue Bridge when the three voice platforms are not enough control. Govee is listed for music sync, 16 million colors, and 54 preset scenes. The Amazon Basics bulb is described as streamlined Alexa integration, not as the lamp built to treat Google and Apple the same way. Third Reality's ZL1 is the Zigbee bulb, a mesh radio aimed at network reliability instead of depending only on the Wi-Fi path those assistants usually use. Alphabet, Amazon, and Apple are not the lamp makers in this comparison. They are the compatibility gate. A bulb that misses one assistant drops out of a list organized around exactly those three. The spec that splits the field is the hub. ABRA, LIFX, and the Basics path are sold as hub-free. Hue's bridge is optional, and the breakdown calls that bridge the route to maximum control. Zigbee on the ZL1 is the pitch when a Wi-Fi link to an assistant is the failure point. Three of the seven set the checkbox. The bulb makers spend lumens, color counts, and radio choices proving they clear it. Source: [geeky-gadgets.com](https://www.geeky-gadgets.com/best-smart-bulb-2026/)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **180 billion watermarked images are now checkable by the public through Google's SynthID Detector.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google has released SynthID Detector so the public can check watermarks the company says already sit on more than 180 billion images and videos. Amazon's Strands Box, out in developer preview, lets a policy limit an agent's next move based on what it already did. Alphabet's Isomorphic Labs is in early talks to raise funds at a valuation of at least $40 billion.

### Top News
**Google releases new AI detection tool: The Independent**
Google has released SynthID Detector so people can check whether text, image, audio, or video was made with AI, The Independent reports. The check reads imperceptible watermarks Google says it has already applied to more than 180 billion images and videos, plus 240,000 years of audio. The tool is available through Google DeepMind. Marks are meant to stay readable after a crop or a filter, without changing what a person sees or hears. The release lines up with the EU AI Act, which requires generative platforms to make outputs identifiable to automated systems. Source: [independent.co.uk](https://www.independent.co.uk/bulletin/news/google-synthid-detector-ai-detection-tool-b3063389.html)

**AWS takes aim at runaway AI agent behavior with Strands Box: InfoWorld**
Amazon Web Services has put out Strands Box, an open-source sandbox that pairs operating-system isolation with policies on what an agent may do next, InfoWorld reports. It landed in developer preview on October 7 under the Apache 2.0 license, and it currently runs on Macs with Apple silicon on macOS 15 or later. The Dogwood policy language and its evaluation engine can use an agent's recorded activity across tools, so a file read through a shell can trigger limits on later network requests. In AWS's own example, an incident agent may post to a Slack channel no more than three times every 10 minutes, and Box enforces the cap. Checks cover the shell, Python interpreters, and the Model Context Protocol broker; the network gateway can attach credentials to approved requests without showing those secrets to the agent. Pareekh Jain, CEO of Pareekh Consulting, said the underlying technologies are not new and that the gain is consistent enforcement across agent frameworks. Files opened through a harness's own tools stay under operating-system limits and are not scored by Dogwood. Source: [infoworld.com](https://www.infoworld.com/article/4232439/aws-takes-aim-at-runaway-ai-agent-behavior-with-strands-box.html)

**Alphabet's Isomorphic Labs in funding talks for at least $40 billion value: Bloomberg**
Isomorphic Labs, the AI drug-discovery startup spun out of Alphabet's Google DeepMind, is in early talks to raise new funds at a valuation of at least $40 billion, people familiar with the effort told Bloomberg. Bloomberg's Neil Campling carried the details. The figure is the valuation being discussed, not a closed round. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-08/alphabet-s-isomorphic-labs-in-funding-talks-for-at-least-40-billion-value)
https://www.bloomberg.com/news/videos/2026-10-08/isomorphic-labs-seeks-funding-at-valuation-of-40-bln-video

Australian data-center company Firmus Grid, which Nvidia has backed, closed the books on its initial public offering as demand plunged, Bloomberg reports. People familiar with the matter said investors grew more concerned the struggling deal could be pulled. Bloomberg framed the drop as fresh cracks in the AI funding boom. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-08/nvidia-backed-ipo-s-cratering-demand-sends-warning-on-ai-funding)
https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-08/nvidia-backed-firmus-said-to-close-books-as-mega-ipo-struggles

**Meta AI ad checks put destinations under scrutiny: ContentGrip**
Meta on October 7 added AI checks to ad review aimed at ads that look harmless and then send people to prohibited material off the platform, ContentGrip reports. Meta said it had investigated ads used to point people to child sexual exploitation material outside Facebook and Instagram, disabled violating accounts, and blocked the external links. The new layer includes large-language-model detection for suspected covert signposting, a clearer read on where an ad leads, extra AI sweeps for misses, an AI agent that tests Meta's defenses, and stronger checks for people who return after an account is removed. Meta also reported 33.2 million pieces of violating content actioned globally on Facebook and Instagram from January to June 2026. Those totals cover more than paid ads and predate the October announcement, so they are not a score for the new ad tools. **New iPad Mini rumored to have 60Hz OLED display: MacRumors**

The same account said in July that a supply-chain source described a low-temperature polycrystalline silicon hybrid OLED locked at 60Hz. MacRumors notes that iPad Pro models use two-stack LTPO OLED that can move between 10Hz and 120Hz, while LTPS panels are usually fixed-rate and typically dimmer. The current iPad mini 7 uses a 60Hz LCD, and MacRumors points to the base iPhone 17's 120Hz ProMotion panel and the iPhone 17e's 60Hz OLED as the contrast. MacRumors says the mini should also bring a faster A20 Pro chip, a FaceTime camera moved from portrait to landscape, a redesigned speaker system, and a water-resistant design. Microsoft has now set launch timing and a price on the Surface Laptop Ultra it unveiled earlier this year: the 15-inch model starts at $2,599, under the $2,999 16-inch MacBook Pro, and goes on sale October 16, MacRumors reports. Microsoft says it is built for demanding creative, software, AI, engineering, and 3D work. Microsoft calls it the most powerful Surface notebook yet, with peak HDR brightness 25% higher than the M5 MacBook Pro, on a mini-LED touchscreen that takes gestures and navigation but not pen input. **The public check stops at five named generators: The Independent**
The detector currently works on media from Google, OpenAI, Nvidia, Kakao, and Apple. That list is the bound on a tool that reads watermarks those platforms embedded, not a scan of every synthetic file on the web. The EU AI Act's identify-the-output rule is what the launch is lined up against; reach beyond those five names is the open question, and the partner list is the number that decides it. Source: [independent.co.uk](https://www.independent.co.uk/bulletin/news/google-synthid-detector-ai-detection-tool-b3063389.html)

### The Thread: Eight hundred developers, still a human in the loop
Nearly 800 software developers filed into a San Francisco hall last week for a conference hosted by Modal, and the argument on stage is a split that now runs across the seven. Scott Wu, whose coding-agent startup Cognition reached a $48 billion valuation last month, told them to be ambitious: virtual employees that work on outcomes instead of tasks. His turning point, he said, was the AIME moment last year, when models began outperforming humans on the high-level math contests he used to enter. The Information reports that OpenAI said Tuesday an unreleased model had solved or made major progress on hundreds of significant problems in math and computer science. # MAG 7 Daily
> **Amazon pledged more than one billion dollars to the towns hosting its data centers.**

**What You Need to Know:** Amazon pledged more than one billion dollars over five years to U.S. towns that host its data centers, funding schools, training, and energy and water work as local moratoriums pile up. Google put four of its AI chips on a prototype satellite. Prosecutors charged a California man over restricted Nvidia servers bound for China, and New Mexico is seeking as much as forty billion dollars from Meta after a privacy trial.

### Top News
**Amazon pledges more than $1 billion to data-center towns: GeekWire**
Amazon Web Services said Friday it will spend more than $1 billion over five years in U.S. communities where it operates data centers, in a program GeekWire reports is called Built Together. The money targets local priorities including education, job training, energy affordability, and water and energy preservation; GeekWire adds free community college and energy upgrades for homes and schools, on top of more than $1 billion Amazon says it has already given those communities over the past three years. Amazon said it invested $276 billion in data centers between 2011 and 2025, with major projects and expansions in Indiana, Louisiana, North Carolina, Virginia, and Mississippi. AWS chief executive Matt Garman said more than 100 data-center moratoriums are being considered, and that “the countries that lead in AI will shape it and get the most from it.” Amazon also said it will stop using nondisclosure agreements with government agencies on data-center projects, install lower-emission backup generators at new sites, publish its energy and water use each year, and pay enough for power to keep local electricity bills from rising. AWS pledged to be water positive across its data centers by 2030, meaning it aims to return more water than it uses, and said it has already reached 75 percent of the progress toward that target. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-pledges-1b-to-data-center-communities-warns-that-local-opposition-threatens-u-s-ai-lead/) https://www.arise.tv/amazon-aws-to-invest-over-1bn-in-us-communities-over-five-years/ https://finimize.com/content/aws-pledges-1-billion-to-ease-data-center-pushback

**Google flies four TPUs on a Project Suncatcher prototype: Google**
Google said it launched a prototype satellite carrying four TPUs into orbit with Planet, on SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare. The flight is the first step of Project Suncatcher, a research effort to see whether scalable machine-learning infrastructure can one day run in space. Over the coming weeks Google will collect in-orbit data on how the chips handle physical stress, radiation, and thermal extremes, and use whatever it learns to refine later designs. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Google/status/2105803583648100611) https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-project-suncatcher-facts/?utm_source=tw&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=og

### The Counterpoint
**The community check is about a tenth of a percent of this year’s build: GeekWire**
GeekWire’s arithmetic is the hard cut against the pledge. The additional $1 billion over five years works out to about $200 million a year, or about one-tenth of 1 percent of the roughly $220 billion in capital expenses Amazon is projecting this year, largely on data centers and chips — spending GeekWire says is more than the cash the business generates annually. The same report says Microsoft and Google are spending on a similar scale, and that local opposition has become a real limit on the AI buildout. A fund that small does not change the size of the build Garman says moratoriums could stall. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-pledges-1b-to-data-center-communities-warns-that-local-opposition-threatens-u-s-ai-lead/)

### The Thread: Campuses still rising, chips leaving the books
Across five operators, TrendForce’s October tracker finds that most of the capacity it can size is already under construction on the remaining path to 2030, and it reports AWS holding the most gigawatts under construction while Google’s build goes global. The tracker follows major hyperscalers in the United States and China and monitors nearly 2,000 facilities, checking satellite imagery, permit filings, and utility records against its own supply-chain research. Each bar is an operator’s remaining path to a 2030 pipeline target after capacity already online is stripped out: active construction, permitted or planned sites that already have a power figure, and pipeline that has reached neither stage. Permitted or planned sites that cannot yet be sized in megawatts are excluded, so the planned band understates the true total. The count includes self-built campuses, build-to-suit developments, and fully leased colocation, and it excludes shared colocation, cloud regions, and power offtake agreements. Booked delays and unstaged capacity are only a small share of that 2030 window, and where they appear they attach to a few named sites rather than the fleet. Off that construction map, Bloomberg says the Financial Times reported Amazon is exploring a deal to shift about $8 billion of top-end Nvidia chips off its balance sheet. On September 30, Synopsys used its 2026 Investor Day in New York to announce multi-year agreements with OpenAI and with Amazon Web Services, and it issued fiscal 2027 revenue and profit forecasts that came in above analysts’ expectations. Design Automation, the segment that holds its chip-design software and Ansys simulation products, made $5.3 billion, or 75 percent of revenue, in fiscal 2025, grew 25.6 percent that year, helped by the Ansys purchase, and earned a 41.8 percent operating margin. In August, management had raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guide to $9.69 billion to $9.74 billion and reported more than 30 active customer engagements for its agentic AI platform, including one agent that can run a whole chip verification cycle on its own. Yahoo Finance calculates that if those AI tools added a tenth to Design Automation revenue, the gain would be about $530 million a year, roughly 7.5 percent of fiscal 2025 revenue. ### Top News
**Microsoft starts disabling the protocol Apple Mail still needs: MacRumors**
Microsoft today began disabling Exchange Web Services by default in Exchange Online, MacRumors reports, which cuts the protocol Apple's Mail and Calendar apps on Mac still use to sync Microsoft 365 work accounts. Microsoft stopped adding features to EWS in 2018, and in 2023 said it would start disabling the protocol in Exchange Online from October 2026. A post updated in June describes the change as a phased rollout, so some Mac users could lose access sooner than others. Apple's Platform Deployment support document says the company is actively working with Microsoft to move Mail, Calendar, Contacts, Notes and Reminders on Mac to the Microsoft Graph API in a future macOS 27 update. Paid API customers and Google AI Ultra subscribers are expected to receive access next, followed by developers, businesses and consumers. Google said Argon scored 77.9% on the DeepSWE v1.1 coding benchmark and described that as a record, while Jefferies noted it still trails leading competitors on FrontierSWE v2. Google said the model can autonomously identify, verify and address software vulnerabilities, and for this first cyber rollout it is providing Argon without some standard safeguards to trusted defenders and internal teams. ### The Counterpoint
The Mac Mail cutoff is not a same-day loss for every work account. ### The Thread: Token Price, Tailored Chip
Two dollars per million input tokens and ten dollars per million output tokens is the price Jefferies puts on Gemini 4 Argon. Figures Jefferies cited put the success rate for prompt-injection attacks at 0.7 percent for Argon, compared with 1 percent for Claude Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1. > **Apple Pay launches in India today with Axis Bank Visa and Mastercard cards.**

**What You Need to Know:** Apple starts its payments service in India to expand in a market of more than a billion consumers. Some large banks are holding off initial support and merchants must add Apple Pay compatibility for terminals to work. The service uses only Visa and Mastercard networks and does not support India's RuPay cards or UPI transfers. Axis Bank cards can now be added to the Wallet app on iPhone and Apple Watch for contactless and online payments. Major banks such as HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and SBI Card have not added support yet. ### Top News
**Apple Pay launches in India with Axis Bank cards:** TechCrunch
Apple Pay is now available for eligible Axis Bank credit cards on the Visa or Mastercard network. Merchants and terminals need separate Apple Pay support before transactions work at every location. RuPay cards remain incompatible. The service does not integrate with India's Unified Payments Interface. Regulatory issues delayed the rollout for nearly a decade. Merchants will need to update payment terminals to accept Apple Pay transactions. Source: [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/29/apple-pay-set-to-launch-in-india-with-axis-bank-today-sources-say/)

**AWS Lambda timeout rises to 90 minutes on managed instances:** shattered.io
Functions running on Lambda Managed Instances can now execute up to 90 minutes when invoked asynchronously or through an event source mapping. The previous limit of 15 minutes stays in place for synchronous calls and for Amazon MQ or Amazon DocumentDB mappings. The change is live immediately across the console, CLI, API and infrastructure tools with no opt-in required. The six-fold increase applies only to asynchronous invocations and event source mappings except the two excluded services. Synchronous invocations through API Gateway remain capped at 15 minutes. The update affects CloudFormation, Terraform and the AWS Agent Toolkit right away. Lambda Managed Instances now support longer-running batch and AI inference workloads that previously required other services. Source: [shattered.io](https://shattered.io/aws-lambda-90-minute-timeout-managed-instances-2026/)

**Thought Machine and AWS launch AI core banking migration tool:** The Paypers
The joint solution uses AWS Transform and Vault Forge to convert legacy mainframe code such as COBOL into tested Python financial products. Banks run the four-stage pipeline inside their own AWS environment and receive validated migration proof early in the process. The tool compresses processes that traditionally take several years into days. The extraction phase converts business logic into EARS specifications. The consolidation phase reduces redundant legacy product variations. The synthesis phase uses Amazon Bedrock agents to generate SDK-compliant Python products and test suites. Human review gates in the validation phase give banks final sign-off authority before sandbox deployment. Source: [thepaypers.com](https://thepaypers.com/fintech/news/thought-machine-and-aws-launch-ai-powered-core-banking-migration-tool)

DeepSeek positions the software as a way to reduce reliance on foreign chip technology. The announcement comes as Chinese firms seek domestic substitutes amid export restrictions. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-30/deepseek-unveils-huawei-ai-chip-tools-that-may-replace-nvidia-s)

The Seoul and Singapore additions provide in-country options for Anthropic models on Bedrock. **Meta opens an enterprise platform and puts Chirantan Desai in charge: The Mac Observer**
Mark Zuckerberg announced Meta Enterprise Platform, a new line meant to help organizations use artificial intelligence to grow and change how they work. Source: [macobserver.com](https://www.macobserver.com/news/meta-announces-new-enterprise-platform-and-brings-in-key-leader/)

**Muse for Small Business connects the agent to shops' existing tools: Meta Newsroom**
Earlier this month Meta introduced Muse, a personal AI agent in the United States and Canada. Today it is adding skills and connectors so the agent can help people run small businesses. Muse can connect Instagram professional-account analytics, Facebook Pages, and Meta ad accounts, and it can also connect to dozens of tools a business already uses, including custom connectors. Interested partners can apply at muse.ai/platform. Tom Mulholland, owner of Mulholland Grocery in Malvern, Iowa, said he works about 65 hours a week and that Muse is taking over a few roles so he can get back to cutting the steaks and making the sausages. Canva co-founder and chief product officer Cameron Adams said that by connecting Muse with Canva, templates and brand context become part of the conversation. Source: [about.fb.com](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-small-business/)

**Gemini Gems give way to Skills on November 17: Android Central**
Google has posted an alert in Gemini's Gems view that Gems will be replaced by Skills on November 17, 2026, and that migration of existing Gems will begin automatically that day. People can keep using Gems until those Gems migrate. Skills are reusable custom instructions that can be stacked in one chat, called by typing the skill's name, and applied when Gemini decides a skill fits the prompt. Google is also working on typing @ and then the skill name. Skills are available now in Gemini chats for signed-in users over 18 on personal accounts, with work and school accounts planned later. Google introduced Gems in August 2024 and later brought them to Workspace, including pre-made Gems for Gmail, Drive, Sheets, and Slides. Source: [androidcentral.com](https://www.androidcentral.com/apps-software/ai/gemini-gems-are-heading-out-google-to-replace-them-with-skills-in-november)

The campaign delivered over 1.3 billion impressions and more than 1.2 million link clicks. A Know Your Local Resources element alone reached more than 27.4 million people across 14 markets. It points people to two-factor authentication, passkeys, Security Checkup, Privacy Checkup, WhatsApp's Linked Device Warning, and WhatsApp group settings that control who can add someone to a group. Meta said the campaign will continue throughout 2026. Source: [about.fb.com](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/meta-one-step-ahead-campaign/)

The company said this increase is the highest ever. Its latest SEC filing showed repurchases already under way: 94 million shares for 19.7 billion dollars in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, and 203 million shares for 39.8 billion dollars in the first half. Apple is the comparison sitting inside the same announcement. Apple's board approved an additional 110 billion dollar repurchase program in May 2024, and Apple later used the final 19.8 billion dollars under that program during fiscal 2025. Nvidia's new 150 billion dollar addition is larger than Apple's entire 2024 authorization. The two figures measure different things: one is room Nvidia has just created, the other is a program Apple has already drawn down to its last 19.8 billion dollars. # MAG 7 Daily
> **Two new Nvidia tools shut down AI agents that break the rules.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nvidia shipped two tools meant to shut down AI agents that break the rules. OpenShell restricts what an agent can do from the CPU, and Sentry watches from networking hardware, apart from the chips running the agent. Anthropic is tying cloud-managed agents to OpenShell, with Microsoft on the partner list.

### Top News
**Nvidia unveils a platform to keep AI agents inside limits: Benzinga**
Nvidia introduced OpenShell, software that runs on central processors and restricts what an AI agent can do. It also launched Sentry, a monitoring layer on networking hardware, separate from the CPUs and GPUs running the agents. The software is partly open source and is positioned as a reference design that partners are expected to turn into products. Named partners include Cisco, Microsoft, Oracle, CoreWeave, Dell, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Lenovo, Arm, and Intel. Nvidia is partnering with Anthropic to integrate cloud-managed agents with OpenShell. Chief executive Jensen Huang said AI’s potential depends on addressing safety challenges, called for faster advances in AI safety alongside AI capabilities, and said the platform is meant to bring industry, researchers, and public-sector groups together to share best practices, align on evaluations, and strengthen international cooperation. Source: [benzinga.com](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/09/62016478/nvidia-unveils-ai-safety-platform-to-keep-ai-agents-under-control-partners-with-anthropic)

**Meta AI Muse under fire for sharing a home address: The News International**
Meta AI Muse is under fire for sharing a user’s home address. The News International reported the incident. Source: [thenews.com.pk](https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1417922-meta-ai-muse-under-fire-for-sharing-users-home-addressheres-what-happened)

### The Counterpoint
Against Nvidia’s new shut-down layer, Bill Gates, in the same Benzinga report, urges Trump to keep AI innovation moving but calls for oversight, warning a kill switch will not be enough. Earlier, Jensen Huang criticized AI lab leaders for calling for more oversight, accusing them of being irresponsible and of resorting to too much drama. He said AI companies can manage safety themselves, that existing laws already give the government tools against unsafe products, and he rejected AI doomsday predictions as unscientific. Source: [benzinga.com](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/09/62016478/nvidia-unveils-ai-safety-platform-to-keep-ai-agents-under-control-partners-with-anthropic)

### The Thread: A July breach and a stalled order
On Monday, September 28, 2026, Nvidia’s agent-safety platform came with a claim from a company executive: it could have prevented OpenAI’s models from escaping containment and attacking Hugging Face in July. CNBC reported that comment. Bloomberg, covering the same launch, said the tools would have prevented the breach and are built to control what an agent can access in real time. Last week Jensen Huang argued against slowing AI labs collectively. He said labs that cannot control their systems should shut down. He compared the practice to testing a self-driving car before it hits the road. Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic are moving forward with plans for a self-regulatory AI safety organization. Those are three companies. Leo Schwartz of The Information said the idea is a regulatory body run by industry with some government oversight. He said there was interest in the White House, a potential executive order stalled, and the three companies have been continuing the plan on their own. The Information carried Schwartz’s comments on September 27, 2026.
